title: High Availability & Disaster Recovery
oneLiner: Meet your RTO and RPO with Route 53 routing, backups, and the four DR strategies.
examWeightNote: Completes Design Resilient Architectures (26% of the exam).
objectives: Define RTO and RPO and map them to the four DR strategies.
Use Route 53 routing policies (failover, latency, weighted, geolocation) and health checks.
Design multi-AZ (HA) vs multi-Region (DR) and know what each protects against.
Apply AWS Backup, snapshots, and cross-Region replication for durability.

services.name: Amazon Route 53
services.purpose: Managed DNS with health checks and routing policies for failover and global traffic steering.

services.name: AWS Backup
services.purpose: Centralized, policy-based backups across many services with cross-Region/-account copy.

services.name: RDS Multi-AZ
services.purpose: Synchronous standby in another AZ with automatic failover for the database tier.

services.name: S3 Cross-Region Replication
services.purpose: Asynchronously replicates objects to a bucket in another Region for DR/compliance.

services.name: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery
services.purpose: Continuously replicates servers to AWS for fast, low-RPO recovery.

keyConcepts: RTO = how long you can be down (recovery time); RPO = how much data you can lose (recovery point). Smaller RTO/RPO costs more.
The four DR strategies, cheapest→fastest: Backup & Restore, Pilot Light, Warm Standby, Multi-Site Active/Active.
Multi-AZ = high availability within a Region (survives AZ failure). Multi-Region = disaster recovery (survives Region failure) and global low latency.
Route 53 failover routing + health checks can automatically redirect traffic to a standby Region/endpoint when the primary is unhealthy.
RDS Multi-AZ is for availability (synchronous standby, auto-failover), not for scaling reads — read replicas handle read scaling.

resources.label: Disaster recovery options in the cloud

scenarios.scenario: A business needs its app to recover in another Region within minutes (low RTO) but wants to avoid paying for a full duplicate of production running all the time.
scenarios.question: Which DR strategy best fits a low-RTO, cost-conscious requirement?

options.label: Warm Standby — a scaled-down but always-running copy that scales up on failover
No DR plan; rely on Multi-AZ

scenarios.explanation: Warm Standby keeps a scaled-down copy always running in the DR Region, so failover is fast (low RTO) at a fraction of the cost of full active/active. Backup & Restore is cheapest but slowest; active/active is fastest but most expensive.

scenarios.scenario: You want DNS to automatically send users to a secondary Region only when the primary application endpoint becomes unhealthy.
scenarios.question: Which Route 53 configuration achieves automatic failover?

options.label: Failover routing policy with health checks on the primary

scenarios.explanation: Failover routing with a health check monitors the primary; when it's unhealthy, Route 53 automatically answers with the secondary endpoint. Weighted/simple routing don't react to health for failover.

quiz.question: What does RPO (Recovery Point Objective) measure?
options: The maximum acceptable amount of data loss, measured in time
The number of Availability Zones used
The cost of the DR site
quiz.answer: The maximum acceptable amount of data loss, measured in time
quiz.explanation: RPO is how much data (in time) you can afford to lose. RTO is how long you can be down. Together they drive DR strategy choice.

quiz.question: Which DR strategy is the cheapest but has the longest recovery time?
quiz.explanation: Backup & Restore stores backups and rebuilds on demand — lowest cost, highest RTO/RPO. Active/active is fastest and most expensive.

quiz.question: RDS Multi-AZ primarily provides which benefit?
options: High availability via a synchronous standby with automatic failover
Global low-latency reads in every Region
quiz.answer: High availability via a synchronous standby with automatic failover
quiz.explanation: Multi-AZ keeps a synchronous standby in another AZ and fails over automatically. To scale reads you add read replicas, which is a separate feature.

quiz.question: You need to protect against an entire AWS Region failing. What should you implement?
options: A multi-Region architecture with data replication
More frequent EBS snapshots in the same Region
quiz.answer: A multi-Region architecture with data replication
quiz.explanation: Surviving a whole-Region outage requires replicating data and capacity to another Region (DR). Multi-AZ only protects against AZ-level failures.
